summary: Iron County, MI tower in the Ottawa National Forest, listed standing and not removed; a 1943 newspaper report names one of its tower watchers. Build date and access not found.

facts.design: lattice observation tower (OpenStreetMap tags); Michigan listing has a 'T. Cabin: no' field with the abbreviation unexplained

events.note: Mary Scalcucci took over the job from her husband, who had manned the tower for eight years; she was one of four women tower watchers employed by the conservation department (Escanaba Daily Press, June 13, 1943, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)

evidence.supports: one of four women tower watchers employed by the conservation department
evidence.quote: one of the four women employed as tower watchers by the conservation department

evidence.supports: husband manned the tower eight years
evidence.quote: which her husband manned for eight years

evidence.supports: husband released to be fire warden in Crystal Falls
evidence.quote: to release him to act as fire warden in Crystal Falls

evidence.supports: she took over the Bates job from her husband
evidence.quote: Mrs. Scalcucci took over her present job of forest fire spotting in the Bates tower

corrections.why: The Michigan listing gives PID(s) RL1564, a survey identifier in the same format as the NGS PIDs on the Forest Lookouts pages, so 'NGS None' looks wrong

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder, or height found. The only dated history is the 1943 staffing quote, which we read through the Forest Lookouts page (the original newspaper was not reached). The 'T. Cabin: no' field is unexplained, so the design line is cautious. The Michigan history page (michiganfiretower.com/history/) appeared in search only and was not read. The 'NGS None' register value in the brief looks wrong (see corrections). Access unknown, so no access or visit facts are recorded; the freelibrary article on 1940s lookouts returned 403 and was not read.
